summary: Scenario 2 final validation on Multi-Part MATCHED SET quote SA-260604-165816 with NEW third set qty 300. Results: (1) The Allocate-By distinctness fix and the LTL minimum notice are VERIFIED WORKING — Board MSF, Equal Split, and By Weight produce three DISTINCT freight tuples that match the spec's expected w/markup values exactly. (2) HOWEVER, the two NEW Matched-Set unified-qty fixes specifically called out in the spec have FAILED: (a) the Per-Item Qty 300 slot still lists ONLY the Header component (not all three), and (b) the Per-Job third scenario header still reads 'Scenario 3' (not 'Qty 300'). RightDashboard.buildItems is NOT actually treating Matched Set's top-level qty 300 as a unified per-component qty when only the Header component has explicit slot[2] data.

ui_bugs.issue: FAIL — Header text reads 'Scenario 3' instead of 'Qty 300'. Spec explicitly required: 'A Per-Job scenario with a single uniform qty is labeled Qty N (not Scenario N).' In Matched Set this third scenario IS a single uniform qty (300), so it should say 'Qty 300'. It still falls back to the generic 'Scenario 3' label. (First two scenarios DO correctly show 'Qty 100' and 'Qty 150'.)

ui_bugs.component: FreightDashModal — Per Job view, scenario 3 component qtys
ui_bugs.issue: Related/root-cause to the two issues above: in the Per-Job Scenario 3 table the rows show Display Base=150, 60ct. Tray=150, Header=300 — i.e. only the Header was updated to qty 300, and the Display Base + 60ct. Tray stayed at their slot[1]=150 qty. The shipment header reads '747 lbs · 3 skids · 13 ft combined' (vs. an expected 'all 3 components at qty 300' shipment). This is the same root bug that breaks Per-Item slot 2 — RightDashboard.buildItems is not actually broadcasting the unified top-level set qty 300 to ALL components when only one component has been edited to add that tier.

critical_code_review_comments: The allocate-by distinctness fix (RightDashboard.buildScenarioMatrix + FreightDashModal.PerJobTable + engine_routes._alloc_job threading shipWeight) is VERIFIED correct: Board MSF, Equal, By Weight all produce three distinct freight tuples that match the spec's expected $ values to the cent (after accounting for the 15% markup column).
LTL minimum notice banner (dash-min-notice) renders correctly with carrier name and dollar amount — copy is clear and reassuring.

HOWEVER, the Matched-Set unified-qty broadcast fix appears to be only PARTIALLY implemented. Per the spec, in Matched Set mode the top-level set qtys ([100,150,300]) should drive ALL components' qty arrays uniformly. Currently when the user adds a 3rd tier (300) via input-qty-2, only the *active* component (Header in this load) gets a real qty-300 row in its components[].qtys[]. Display Base and 60ct. Tray retain their original 2-qty arrays. The bug manifests in both Per-Item slot 2 (only Header) and Per-Job scenario 2 label ('Scenario 3' fallback because non-uniform qtys defeat the 'Qty N' label condition).

Suspected root: RightDashboard.buildItems still iterates per-component qty arrays rather than per top-level set-qty index in Matched Set mode. The fix needs to map top-level qtys (line item 'QTY' row: 100/150/300) → ALL components' working qty per slot, regardless of whether the individual component's qtys[] array has that index populated.

rca of the issue: Bug: In Matched-Set mode with a newly-added 3rd set-qty tier (300), only the Header component had its components[].qtys[2]=300 (because that was the active component when the user clicked input-qty-2). Display Base and 60ct. Tray still have qtys=[100,150]. RightDashboard.buildItems iterates each component's qtys[] independently, so for slot index 2 only Header has a real row — Display Base and 60ct. Tray are absent. Consequence: (a) Per-Item Qty 300 panel shows only Header, (b) Per-Job scenario 2 has non-uniform qtys (150/150/300) and therefore fails the 'all qtys equal' check used to print the 'Qty N' label, falling back to 'Scenario 3'. Fix path: in buildItems for Matched Set mode, iterate the TOP-LEVEL setQtys array (length 3 with [100,150,300]) and broadcast setQtys[slot] to every component's working qty for that slot, ignoring any gaps in per-component qtys[] arrays.
